name: Herbs, spices, and dried seasonings (turmeric, cinnamon, paprika, chili powder, pepper)
native_basis_label: dried spice as placed on the market (dry basis)
scope_note: Covers dried herbs, spices, and dried seasonings (turmeric, cinnamon, paprika, chili powder, pepper, cumin, etc.). Lead is a form_split by EU botanical part (fruit/seed/flower-pistil/bud/root-rhizome/bark). Total chromium and Cr-VI are screened as lead-chromate adulteration co-markers, the defining hazard of this category. Fresh culinary herbs sold fresh route to the produce categories; tea and herbal infusions route to Cat 5 Beverages; salt routes to the salt row.

Pb.basis: dried spice as placed on the market (dry basis)
Pb.instrument: EU Reg. 2023/915 — lead in spices, set by botanical part. The controlling worldwide instrument for spice lead; carried as a form_split and preserved exactly. Certification applies the botanical part matching the spice.

forms.form: fruit spices (paprika, chili powder, black pepper, allspice)

stricter_unselected.scope: Spices (xiang xin liao), except cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, and spice mixtures (GB 2762-2022 Table 1, Lead)

Cd.basis: dried spice (dry basis); spice-specific dried-basis limit. Fresh fruiting-vegetable Cd (50) and fresh-herb Cd (200) are a different, wet-weight basis and do not govern a dried spice.

tAs.basis: dried herbs and spices (dry basis). Fresh-herb tAs (300) is a wet-weight basis and does not govern a dried spice.

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level specific to dried spices (inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation defined for rice and drinking water); dried-spice arsenic is regulated as total arsenic, which arithmetically bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). The New York State DOH 2019 metals-in-spices guidance (nys-doh2019-metals-spices-guidance), routed to this row, reports measurable inorganic arsenic in spices, so the fraction is screened by reflex speciation on the total-As result rather than dismissed as absent. Israel's dried-plant iAs figure (300 ug/kg) is bounded by, and consistent with, the total-As ceiling.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-As speciation on the total-As result; bounded by the tAs cell. No sovereign dried-spice iAs ML.
iAs.trigger: reflex iAs speciation when total arsenic approaches the tAs ceiling

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation with no formation pathway in a terrestrial dried spice, and it is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). Spice mercury is regulated as total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg spice standard (Vietnam, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury spice ML anywhere

Ni.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for dried spices. The EU sets nickel only for fresh herbs (1200 ug/kg) and leafy vegetables (500 ug/kg) on a fresh-weight basis; reading either across to a dried spice would be a basis error (drying concentrates the analyte several-fold), so it would UNDERSTATE a protective standard and is not used. Nickel is screened instead of assigned a mis-based number.
Ni.reference_method: Total-nickel screen (ICP-MS); no dried-spice sovereign ML; EU fresh-herb/leafy-veg nickel limits are fresh-basis and not comparable.
Ni.trigger: periodic nickel screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Sn.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for dried spices (tin MLs govern tinplate-canned product only). Routed sources (cicero2022-minerals-spices-aromatic-herbs, pradhan2023-heracleum-nepalense-elements) report measurable trace tin in dried spices from soil/processing background, so tin is screened rather than dismissed as absent.
Sn.reference_method: Total-tin screen (ICP-MS); no sovereign dried-spice tin ML; the canned-food 250 mg/kg limit is can-only.
Sn.trigger: periodic tin screen; flag on anomalous elevation

Al.rationale: Dried spices are natural aluminium accumulators (aluminium is taken up from soil and concentrated on drying); the aluminium present is background, not contamination. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for spices; dietary aluminium is managed by intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food ML. Matches the existing spices/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
Al.reference_method: Managed by intake vs TWI; periodic screen; no per-food contaminant ML.
Al.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for spices in any credible jurisdiction; managed by TWI
Al.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). For spices this cell is load-bearing as an ADULTERATION SCREEN, not a nutrient check: turmeric and chili powder are adulterated with lead chromate (PbCrO4) to brighten colour, so an elevated total chromium co-occurring with elevated lead is the signature of lead-chromate adulteration. Total chromium is screened and co-read with the lead result.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS), co-read with lead; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: flag when total chromium is elevated and co-occurs with elevated lead (lead-chromate adulteration signature)

Cr-VI.rationale: Lead chromate (PbCrO4) used to adulterate turmeric and chili is a hexavalent-chromium compound, so Cr-VI is NOT dismissed as not-material for spices (unlike inert food matrices where Cr-VI reduces to Cr-III). Where the lead/total-chromium adulteration screen is elevated, reflex Cr-VI speciation confirms the chromate. No sovereign sets a Cr-VI food ML, so this is a screen, not an alignment.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation triggered by the lead-chromate adulteration signature (elevated lead + elevated total chromium).
Cr-VI.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation on the lead-chromate adulteration signature

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved; dried-spice basis discipline)
